name: World Humanoid Robot Games
ability_definition: The ability to quickly move the arms and legs.

task_realism.reasoning: Sprinting is a real, physically embodied task that requires rapid leg cycling, so it genuinely exercises limb speed. Most workplace uses of this ability are different, though. They include striking, throwing, fast reaching and sorting, and quick evasive or protective arm and leg movements. A straight-line 100 m race on a prepared track only resembles a small subset of these, such as athletic or emergency running.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: The robot moves in the real world under a standardized timed protocol with competitive stakes, which is better than simulation. However, the setting is highly controlled: a flat track, a single event and a known course. Whether the robot runs autonomously or under remote guidance is not reported, which makes it unclear how much of the result reflects the system itself. Workplace conditions with varied surfaces, loads and task switching are not represented.

construct_coverage.reasoning: Only the legs are tested, and arm speed, which is central to O*NET's high anchor of throwing punches, is absent. The metric is whole-body forward velocity, which mixes limb movement speed with actuator power, leg length, gait control and balance. Performance over 100 m also contains a small endurance and sustained-output component rather than pure speed of individual movements.

format_match.reasoning: The output is actual physical movement measured by elapsed time, a natural and direct metric for speed with no artificial answer format. The format is still a single sport-style event rather than the discrete, rapid limb actions typical of work tasks, so it only partly matches real work artifacts.

transferability_reasoning: The 100 m humanoid sprint is a genuine, real-world timed test of fast leg movement, which gives it better format and realism than simulated locomotion benchmarks. It omits arm speed entirely and conflates limb speed with hardware power, balance and gait control. The possibility of remote guidance further weakens the link to autonomous capability, so it transfers only partially, as a proxy for running speed rather than general limb speed.

2026.model_or_system: Tiangong Ultra (Beijing Humanoid Robot Innovation Center)
2026.metric: seconds (100 m sprint time; lower is better)
2026.human_reference: General adult workforce. Speed of Limb Movement is a basic physical ability used across manual and physical occupations. Elite sprinters are the ceiling of that population.
